ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Company Registration; PBOC payment institution licensing and AML/CFT rules applicable to electronic money institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Business License for the foreign invested enterprise or existing foreign corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Municipal Market Supervision Administration or foreign company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: notarize before a competent notary public where issued, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China or the relevant foreign designated competent authority; do not add consular legalization. If the document is from a non-Apostille state, use consular legalization at the PRC Embassy/Consulate exclusively.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR/local Market Supervision Administration for domestic entities; Companies Registry or equivalent for foreign corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction for Hague member states; for non-member states, consular legalization solely by the PRC Embassy/Consulate; no sequential combination of both mechanisms.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution before a notary public; then Apostille by the notary's supervising authority in a Hague state, or consular legalization only if the jurisdiction is not an Apostille member; the two routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Joint Venture Contract and Amended Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporating shareholders and directors of the proposed Sino-foreign equity joint venture
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille by the issuing jurisdiction's designated competent authority if the country is a member; otherwise, sole consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate in that non-member state; do not combine Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution of the foreign investor or joint venture's proposed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issuance by the bank, notarization of authorized signatory, then either Hague Apostille by the bank's country competent authority if Apostille member, or consular legalization only for non-member states; apostille and consular legalization are alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, and senior management must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and Chinese domestic restrictive lists issued by MOFCOM, MFA, PBOC and national financial regulatory authorities. The screening process must cover exact and fuzzy name matching, date of birth, nationality, passport number, and politically exposed person status, including domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs, and international organization PEPs. Enhanced due diligence must be performed for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, negative media, sanctions designation, or beneficial owner exercising control through the 25% ownership or control threshold. Screening results must be documented and re-run on an ongoing basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation Enterprise Name Self-Declaration System accessible through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform; public registry portal: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (https://www.gsxt.gov.cn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name of a Sino-foreign equity joint venture must be in standardized simplified Chinese characters and generally consist of four tiers: administrative division; unique trade name; industry or business characteristics; and organizational form (limited liability company). Foreign-invested enterprises may use a transliterated pinyin rendering of the foreign shareholder's trade name; alphabet letters are permitted only as an approved abbreviation or in the registered English secondary name. The Chinese name is authoritative; the English name must be submitted as supplementary information and must not conflict with existing trademarks. Names must not contain numerals, symbols, misleading words, or state-approved sensitive tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may either revise and resubmit the name through the SAMR online portal, or file a written administrative reconsideration request with the immediately superior market regulation administration within 60 days of receiving the rejection decision. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, the rejected name, the amended name, identity documents, and a legal memorandum demonstrating compliance with the Enterprise Name Registration Measures and the four-tier naming rule. The reviewing authority must issue a decision within 60 days. If reconsideration fails, the applicant may bring administrative litigation within 6 months. Pre-clearance from the competent ministry is required when sensitive tokens are retained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a licensed electronic money institution under ISIC 6619, virtual office/commercial mailbox is rejected outright by SAMR, tax authorities, PBOC, and commercial banks. A physical office in the same city as the registered address is mandatory, with a term lease, dedicated compliance and IT staff, and local operations. Tax authorities compare registered office, tax registration, and actual business place; mismatch triggers forced de-registration and invalidation of the payment institution license. Banks will not open operating accounts for a company using a virtual mailbox.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office checklist includes: valid lease contract, stamp tax paid, physical company plaque, office utilities, attendance records, server room or hosted infrastructure agreement, board meeting minutes, statutory books and records, payroll and social insurance records, and IT disaster recovery plan. Quantified risk: 80% unannounced inspection within 12 months after payment-institution license issuance; 50% during first registration year for shell-company anti-fraud checks; 35% annual random tax inspection; municipal tax bureau may coordinate with SAMR.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fixed fee under the Apostille Convention or consular tariff schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registry certified extract fee, bank administrative fee, and statutory notarial/apostille charges

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 23-37 (establishment and registration), 44-58 (governance and board duties), 81-90 (registered capital and shareholder liability); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4-6 and 15-16; Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law of the PRC; Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Non-bank Payment Institutions (State Council Order No. 773, effective 1 May 2024), Articles 6-18.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Enterprise Registration Division, State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local municipal or provincial Market Supervision Administration; online submission through the SAMR integrated national enterprise registration portal and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application Form for Company Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise together with the adopted Articles of Association; issued instrument is the Business License of the People's Republic of China.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No universal paid-up minimum applies to a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture under the 2023 Company Law. However, because the entity will operate as an electronic money institution issuing virtual IBANs and managing digital wallet reserves, the PBOC imposes a special capital floor: for a payment institution with nationwide electronic-money and settlement services, minimum paid-up registered capital is RMB 100,000,000 (USD equivalent at the prevailing PBOC mid-rate) and must be fully paid in cash before the payment license is granted. The entire paid-in capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account maintained with a PBOC-approved commercial bank; the funds may not be withdrawn, pledged, offset, or applied to losses without prior written PBOC approval and a further board resolution following license issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_JV_LTD (THE 'COMPANY')

The Board of Directors, being lawfully convened and holding the quorum required under the Articles of Association and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), hereby unanimously adopts the following resolutions effective immediately upon the registration of the Company.

RESOLVED, THAT the formation and registration of the Company as a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture under the Foreign Investment Law and the Company Law be and they are hereby ratified and confirmed. The subscriptions to the share capital as set forth in the register of shareholders be and they are hereby approved, consisting of an authorized and registered capital of RMB 100,000,000 divided into 100,000,000 ordinary shares of RMB 1.00 each, with each subscriber required to pay the amount subscribed in cash or in contribution assets acceptable under the Articles of Association and the PBOC capital escrow rules. Until the payment institution license is issued, all paid-in capital shall remain blocked in a designated escrow account at a PBOC-approved commercial bank, free of pledges, encumbrances or withdrawals, and any release shall require a further resolution of the Board and the prior written consent of the People's Bank of China.

RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the registered office of the Company at the address specified in the Business License be and is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory registered office for service of process, official notices and correspondence, and the Legal Representative be and is hereby directed to execute the lease, building occupation certificate, and related documents and to register the address with the State Administration for Market Regulation. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the following persons be and are hereby appointed as the Company's first statutory officers: [insert name of legal representative/executive director], [insert name of general manager], [insert name of chief financial officer], [insert name of AML/CFT compliance officer], and [insert name of auditor], each to serve until removed or replaced by a subsequent resolution of the Board. The Legal Representative shall have all powers granted by the Articles of Association, the CFO shall be responsible for financial administration and statutory filing, and the AML/CFT Officer shall exercise the duties under the Anti-Money Laundering Law and PBOC regulations.

RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT the Chairman, the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly or severally, be and are hereby authorized to open, maintain, transfer and close bank accounts, including the operating account, settlement reserve account and escrow capital account, and to execute all bank mandates, signature cards and clearing documentation. RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT any director, officer or external counsel designated by the Board be and is hereby authorized to execute and file with SAMR, PBOC, the tax authorities and other competent governmental bodies all applications, affidavits, financial statements and accompanying exhibits necessary to implement and give legal effect to the resolutions herein. All preceding resolutions are effective nunc pro tunc as of the date of the Company's establishment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Foreign-Invested Enterprise Pre-registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Service Portal and local Market Supervision Administration enterprise registration division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed legal name of CN_JV_LTD in the approved English transliteration together with shareholder identity documents, proposed business scope mapped to ISIC 6619, and a brief investment plan. The SAMR online system will screen identical or confusingly similar names against the national enterprise name database. After reservation, complete the foreign-invested enterprise information registration in the same portal, including foreign investor jurisdiction, capital contribution currency, beneficial ownership, and registered address. All documents must be uploaded in PDF/A, electronically signed by each subscribing shareholder or an authorized representative, and any foreign corporate shareholder certificate and board authorization must be notarized, apostilled or legalized by the Chinese consulate, and accompanied by a licensed translation into English if required by the accepting officer.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business scope on the standard name-reservation form
Passport or national identity card of each individual subscriber
Certificate of incorporation and board authorization for each foreign corporate shareholder
Power of attorney appointing the formation agent
Registered address lease agreement or ownership certificate with floor-plan
Initial investment and capital contribution schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file an amended name application within five business days using a differentiated secondary name or attach letters of consent from prior right holders. If the foreign-invested enterprise pre-registration is queried, correct the portal data within seven business days and resubmit. If the query persists, request a written refusal statement from SAMR and pursue administrative reconsideration within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Joint Venture Contract, Articles of Association, and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel, licensed notary office, and later SAMR establishment filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the bilingual legal-entity documents, namely the Joint Venture Contract, the Articles of Association, and the shareholders' investment and governance agreement, containing provisions on share capital allocation, subscription timetable, board size and voting, appointment of legal representative and supervisors, capital escrow, deadlock resolution, transfer restrictions, anti-money-laundering and information-security responsibilities, and liquidation rights. Every shareholder must execute the documents before a notary where personal presence is required. The Articles of Association must reflect the mandatory governance rules of the 2023 Company Law and the PBOC payment-license requirements, particularly the blocking of customer payment reserve funds and escrowed registered capital, the fit-and-proper qualifications of directors, and the appointment of an AML/CFT compliance officer. Counsel should certify that the legalization and translation of foreign shareholder documents are complete before submission to SAMR.
required_dossiers: Joint Venture Contract signed by all shareholders
Articles of Association in the approved format
Shareholder resolutions approving the JV structure
Notarized and legalized identity and authorization documents for foreign shareholders
Legal opinion confirming lawful business scope as electronic money and payment services
Proposed list of first directors, supervisors, and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or SAMR determines that an executed document is defective, obtain a written query notice and correct the specific deficiency within seven business days. If a governance clause conflicts with PBOC licensing standards, seek a supplemental shareholders' resolution and re-execute the Article before resubmission. If foreign corporate authorization is insufficient, obtain a fresh board resolution and re-legalize through the relevant consular post.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Establishment Registration and Issuance of the Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration integrated one-stop company registration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for establishment registration through the SAMR integrated online portal, attaching the approved name reservation certificate, executed Joint Venture Contract, Articles of Association, first board resolution, registered-office proof, legal representative and supervisor identification, and the paid-in capital escrow confirmation. The registry will examine the application for statutory completeness, legal name compliance, registered capital schedule, and lawful business scope. Upon approval, the local Market Supervision Administration will issue the Business License with a unified social credit code and concurrently carry out tax registration, social insurance registration, statistical reporting, and customs registration formalities through the multi-integration mechanism. The company must then arrange engraving of the company seal at a licensed seal engraving enterprise and complete foreign-exchange registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange within the statutory period.
required_dossiers: Name reservation acceptance letter
Application Form for Company Establishment Registration
Notarized Joint Venture Contract and Articles of Association
Shareholder resolutions and First Board Resolution
Proof of legal address and lease registration certificate
Identity documents of legal representative, supervisor, directors, and company secretary
Capital contribution bank proof or escrow account issuance confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is suspended, the market administration will issue a correction notice identifying the missing or irregular dossier; the applicant has fifteen business days to upload cured documents online. If the legal representative or supervisor fails the compliance background review, propose a substitute by board resolution and re-file. If the integrated filing encounters a cross-department conflict, request an administrative coordination session at the enterprise legal service window to obtain a manual resolution and written clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Capital Deposit, and Statutory Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: PBOC-approved commercial bank; licensed certified public accounting firm; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Business License, open the company's basic deposit account, general operating account, payment-settlement reserve account, and the blocked escrow capital account at a PBOC-approved commercial bank. Each subscriber must transfer the subscribed RMB capital from its own account in the agreed currency, and the bank must record the funds as escrowed and non-releasable until PBOC authorizes release. A licensed CPA firm must then verify the paid-in capital and issue a statutory capital verification report that will be attached to the PBOC license application. The escrowed capital cannot be pledged, withdrawn, or commingled with customer reserve funds. If the foreign shareholder injects foreign currency, the company must complete SAFE foreign-exchange registration and convert the contribution into RMB at a designated bank, preserving all remittance receipts and source-of-funds documentation.
required_dossiers: Business License and unified social credit code certificate
Articles of Association and First Board Resolution
Completed bank account application forms and signature cards
Original capital contribution receipts and SWIFT or domestic remittance slips
CPA engagement letter and capital verification request
Beneficial ownership declaration and identity documents of account signatories
Escrow account agreement with the PBOC-approved bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening on compliance grounds, provide an enhanced beneficial ownership declaration and documented source of funds; if the proposed escrow institution is not PBOC-approved, select another clearing bank from the approved list. If the CPA declines to issue a capital verification report because contributions are incomplete, procure payment of the deficit or obtain a shareholders' resolution adjusting the contribution timetable. If SAFE questions the foreign-exchange settlement, submit the FIE registration certificate and original remittance documentation to the local SAFE branch within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for PBOC Non-bank Payment Institution License for Electronic Money and Virtual IBAN Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: People's Bank of China, Payment Services Division and relevant PBOC provincial branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the license application under the Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Non-bank Payment Institutions and PBOC implementing circulars, covering issuance of electronic money, digital wallet reserve management, virtual IBAN assignment, and access to central-bank clearing. The dossier must demonstrate a detailed payment-business model, a segregated customer-reserve management scheme, an AML/CFT internal-control manual, information-security and business-continuity frameworks, technology architecture for IBAN generation and wallet accounting, and fit-and-proper certifications for senior management. PBOC will conduct a pre-licensing document review, beneficial-owner and director interviews, and an onsite inspection to verify the operational systems and data-protection controls. Upon approval, PBOC will issue the Payment Business License, after which the company must connect to the designated payment clearing infrastructure and complete all system certifications before commencing live electronic-money issuance.
required_dossiers: PBOC payment business license application form
AML/CFT compliance manual and appointment certificate of the compliance officer
Information security, cyber-risk and business continuity management manuals
Detailed business plan for virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management
Paid-in capital verification report and escrowed capital certificate
Audited financial projections and capital-maintenance plan
Senior management resumes, qualification certificates and criminal record certificates
Corporate governance chart and board resolutions approving licensed operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PBOC issues a supplementary-material query, respond within twenty working days with the precise missing items. If the application is refused due to deficient fit-and-proper requirements or capital inadequacy, appoint replacement directors or senior officers by board resolution and reapply after curing the deficiency, with a minimum cooling-off period of six months. If a denial is based on erroneous facts, engage external counsel to request administrative reconsideration within sixty days under the Administrative Reconsideration Law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) Payment Services Division; no industrial licensing or manufacturing board applies because ISIC 6619 is a financial services activity rather than manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: PBOC Payment Business License (Non-bank Payment Institution Permit) for Electronic Money Issuance and Digital Wallet/Virtual IBAN Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the PRC would be the relevant agency only if physical construction or industrial emission sources existed, which is not the case for a pure financial technology entity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA, Environmental Registration, or exemption certificate is required for the digital electronic-money and virtual IBAN business because no manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, warehousing, effluent discharge, VOC emission or land disturbance will occur.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions and zero hazardous-waste generation; office operations must comply only with municipal solid-waste segregation, electronic-waste recycling, and ordinary office-occupancy health standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for heavy industrial civil-defense permits, but the registered office must obtain the standard fire-safety inspection or occupancy-fire-safety filing from the local Fire and Rescue Bureau for commercial premises. The technology infrastructure supporting electronic-money issuance must satisfy PBOC cybersecurity requirements and ISO 27001 or equivalent data-security certification. Workplace safety training and emergency response procedures must comply with the Work Safety Law for office-based employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic filing is performed on the STA Electronic Tax Administration portal and e-invoice clearance is performed on the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Within 30 days after the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues the business license of the Sino-foreign equity joint venture, the JV must complete taxpayer registration with the competent STA office. Under the integrated market registration system, the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on the business license is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration identifier; no separate TIN certificate is issued. The procurement procedure includes: (i) submission of the SAMR business license, joint venture contract, articles of association, registered-address proof, legal representative identification, finance officer identification, basic account-opening certificate from a Chinese bank, and expected business scope; (ii) confirmation of the tax filing period (monthly or quarterly) and taxpayer type (small-scale or general VAT taxpayer); and (iii) activation of the VAT invoice system on the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform. A foreign non-resident enterprise with no establishment in mainland China that receives Chinese-source income requiring withholding must apply separately to the competent STA branch for a non-resident taxpayer identification number, submit its incorporation certificate and a copy of the underlying Chinese contract, and appoint a withholding agent; this non-resident TIN is distinct from the resident JV's USCC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide check-the-box elections, pass-through elections, or hybrid mismatch elections. A Sino-foreign equity joint venture is a resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law and is separately taxed on worldwide taxable income; group consolidation for income tax purposes is not available. For VAT purposes only, the JV may elect small-scale taxpayer status while annual taxable sales do not exceed RMB 5,000,000, or may elect general taxpayer status, but this is an invoicing and credit-collection mechanism rather than an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT); the general goods rate is 13%, the construction/transport/agricultural rate is 9%, and the financial-services and other-services rate is 6%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No value-added tax registration threshold applies to a newly incorporated PRC legal entity; tax registration is mandatory within 30 days of the business license regardless of revenue. The general VAT taxpayer compulsory threshold is annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000. Below that threshold the JV may be a small-scale taxpayer and may qualify for a preferential monthly VAT exemption of up to RMB 100,000 (RMB 300,000 per quarter); however, as a licensed electronic money institution generating fee income, the JV should obtain general taxpayer status to be able to issue VAT special invoices and recover input VAT on operating costs. Supplies of financial and payment services are taxable at 6% unless zero-rated as qualified exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform as the mandatory clearing system for e-invoices. Newly established enterprises must use the platform or an STA-certified tax-control device before issuing any VAT invoice; each invoice is assigned a unique invoice code and number, is affixed with an anti-fraud digital stamp, and is transmitted to STA in real time. Fully digitalised electronic invoices carry a structured data file (XML) and are automatically reconciled against the taxpayer's VAT return, customs data, and banking records. High-volume licensed financial institutions may access the STA electronic invoice API to batch create, stamp, and report invoices; offline invoices or private-format fiscal documents are not recognised for VAT input credit or export zero-rating purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, export zero-rating is available only where the goods are physically declared to and cleared by Chinese Customs as exported, the exporter receives the sales proceeds from outside China, and the transaction is supported by a valid export contract and commercial invoice. For services, qualifying cross-border services supplied wholly to non-resident recipients and consumed entirely outside mainland China may be zero-rated or VAT-exempt; the JV must demonstrate that the recipient is outside China, the service is not used in China, and the consideration is paid by non-residents through designated foreign-exchange banks. For virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet payment-processing fees, the zero-rating claim will be accepted only if the STA's place-of-supply rules and the cross-border service zero-rating filing requirements for licensed financial institutions are satisfied; any service that facilitates a domestic Chinese payment or is consumed in China remains taxable at 6%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export goods customs declaration form) issued by the General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China showing that the goods physically departed China and identifying the JV as the exporter
Bill of Lading, airway bill, railway waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing delivery to a destination outside mainland China

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or the designated bank's foreign-exchange income declaration and export-proceeds receipt record confirming that the export consideration was collected in convertible currency from a non-resident payer
Export sales contract and commercial invoice matching the commodity description, quantity, price, and payment terms
VAT invoice and the corresponding export VAT zero-rating/refund declaration schedule filed with the STA
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, Customs, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange match e-invoice data, customs declaration data, logistics data, and banking receipts before export zero-rating is honoured. If a zero-rating claim is found to be fraudulent or unsupported, the STA will retroactively claw back the refunded VAT, impose a daily overdue surcharge of 0.05% on the amount underpaid, and impose an administrative fine of one to five times the falsely refunded amount under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. In serious cases, criminal liability for fraudulently obtaining export tax refunds may be pursued, with imprisonment and fines for the responsible individuals; the taxpayer's credit rating may be downgraded and its access to e-invoicing and future export refund facilitation may be suspended. Where fraudulent misrepresentation is established, the ordinary three-year assessment limitation does not bar recovery for the periods under investigation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBoC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime in which current account transactions are convertible after authenticity verification of the underlying trade or service, while capital account transactions remain subject to case-by-case SAFE registration, designated bank accounts, and strict post-entry use monitoring. For this Sino-foreign equity joint venture, the registered capital injection must first complete the SAFE foreign direct investment registration before any inbound remittance can be credited to a foreign currency capital account. Once settled, the proceeds enter an RMB capital account and are ring-fenced for genuine operational expenditures within the approved business scope. The electronic-money institution business model additionally triggers PBoC payment oversight because the virtual IBAN and digital wallet float must be segregated from the JV corporate treasury, and client funds cannot be treated as free corporate money. Dividend remittances are permitted after statutory audit and tax clearance, but require board approval, audited financial statements, tax payment proof, and SAFE cross-border payment filing, and the bank will independently verify the economic substance of the profit behind each distribution. In practice, current account convertibility for trade-backed flows such as merchant settlement, platform service fees, and software development costs is manageable, but any attempt to pass e-money client balances through the corporate capital account would be rejected as speculative or commingled. Overall, the treasury must operate with full SAFE/PBoC documentation discipline and treat capital and current account convertibility as two separate regulatory rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to a domestic designated foreign exchange bank account; China no longer imposes a fixed compulsory surrender ratio for general merchandise receipts. A Class-A trade enterprise may retain receipts in foreign currency or convert them to RMB voluntarily at the market exchange rate, while Class-B and Class-C enterprises face heightened authenticity checks and may need to present, on a transaction-by-transaction basis, export customs declarations, logistics documents, invoices, and the banks electronic verification records. Although the historical 90-day export collection verification timeline has been replaced by SAFEs dynamic trade-in-goods monitoring system, banks still require that the foreign currency repatriation occur within commercially reasonable settlement terms and that any overdue receivable be justified with documentary evidence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs. Offshore EMIs cannot legally maintain domestic settlement accounts, issue domestic IBANs, or provide RMB clearing services directly to this China-based JV unless they hold a valid Payment Business License issued by the PBoC and complete the relevant SAFE filing for cross-border payments. In practice, offshore EMIs are limited to acting as white-label correspondent front-ends that route instructions to Chinese tier-one banks; their inability to demonstrate local licensing, reserve segregation, and SAFE reporting makes them unsuitable for capital escrow, FX surrender, and operational clearing. The JV treasury should instead contract directly with a licensed domestic bank and, if necessary, establish a wholly-owned licensed non-bank payment subsidiary for e-money reserve management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for corporate account opening. The statutory legal representative, or a board-appointed authorized representative holding a notarized and Chinese-consulate-legalized power of attorney, must attend at least one in-branch interview at the chosen tier-one bank for biometric verification, original document inspection, seal filing, and activation of both the capital account and basic deposit account. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted for new foreign-invested enterprise capital accounts; some banks allow online pre-submission of forms, but the final face-to-face verification must happen on Chinese soil before account activity commences.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border ownership chain with intermediate holding companies and nominee shareholder structures obscuring the ultimate beneficial owners of the JV
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal entity chart showing each shareholder and intermediate holding company; certificates of incorporation and registers of directors for all entities in the chain; audited financial statements for the last three years; notarized passports or government-issued IDs of all identified UBOs; share registers and share certificates; executed UBO declaration and source-of-wealth statement; FATCA/CRS self-certification forms; and external counsel legal opinion confirming the validity of the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High or unexplained transaction volume expected from digital wallet and virtual IBAN operations, raising risk of commingled client funds and unidentifiable merchant counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PBoC payment business license application or license certificate; AML compliance program and transaction monitoring policy; independent audit report on internal controls over client funds; merchant onboarding KYC files including business licenses, tax registration, UBO declarations, bank account evidence, and transaction history; anti-fraud and sanctions screening rules; and a Chinese licensed banks written confirmation of the proposed settlement account architecture and reserve segregation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, or controlling director is a politically exposed person or a resident of a FATF high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Curated PEP and sanctions risk declaration; detailed source-of-funds analysis prepared by external counsel; professional bank references from at least two regulated financial institutions; tax residence certificates and good-standing certificates; negative media and litigation search summary; sworn affidavit of legitimate wealth origin; and enhanced due diligence reports on all related bank relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound registered capital remittances sourced from third-party or mixed corporate/personal bank accounts rather than the named foreign investors own regulated account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investors audited financial statements and board resolution approving the equity injection; twelve full months of bank statements from the remitting institution; notarized and legalized constitutive documents of the investor; completed SAFE foreign direct investment registration and capital account opening notice; source-of-wealth documentation for the remitted funds; and PRC certified public accountant capital verification report issued after settlement into the RMB capital account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound registered capital must flow only after SAFE FDI registration and the opening of a designated foreign currency capital account at an authorized tier-one bank. The wire should be sent by the named foreign investor from its own regulated account, with SWIFT field 70 clearly identifying the JV name, investor name, and equity injection purpose. The receiving bank then files the receipt through SAFEs foreign exchange receipt and payment declaration system using the direct investment equity capital transaction purpose code, after which funds may be settled into the RMB capital account. All disbursements from the capital account must match the approved business purpose; a PRC licensed CPA must subsequently issue a capital verification report to confirm that the registered capital has been fully paid and recorded, and the report must be kept with the banks compliance file for future repatriation, audit, and deregistration procedures.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for standard payments to verified overseas suppliers, documentary collections for lower-trust transactions where the JV retains shipping document control, and commercial letters of credit opened by the JVs banker when the counterparty requires bank payment undertaking. Every instruction must carry truthful contract, invoice, customs and logistics references so the bank can complete SAFE goods-trade or services-trade authenticity verification; all RMB cross-border settlements may also clear through CIPS, while foreign currency payments use SWIFT and the domestic banks clearing network. The treasury must maintain audit-ready files for three years to support each clearing rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD and CNY/EUR forward contracts with SAFE-authorized tier-one banks, limited to hedge known current-account exposures;
Cross-currency interest rate and principal swaps for long-term capital raising and investment in the e-money platform, subject to real-exposure and maturity-matching documentation;
Structured FX options such as collars and participating forwards used for cost-effective hedging of forecast trade settlement flows, with no speculative leverage;

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for onshore corporate hedging; hedging must use deliverable onshore products, although an offshore parent may independently enter into NDFs outside China without contaminating the JVs local clearing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Disclosure Report (Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of the calendar year following each reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish by June 30 places the entity on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days; remaining abnormal for three consecutive years moves the entity to the List of Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprises and ultimately permits administrative revocation of the business registration. No monetary fine applies for late filing alone, but strike-off/deregistration is the residual enforcement trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Information Report (foreign-invested enterprise annual reporting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) under the joint MOFCOM/SAMR annual reporting mechanism, filed through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of the year following each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit, or submission of false or omitted information, results in a rectification order from the commerce department; refusal to rectify may incur a fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 (approximately USD 14,000 to USD 70,000), together with inclusion on the abnormal operations list.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) - competent local tax bureau of the entity's registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 following the end of each fiscal year, within five calendar months of the year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing sanctions include a penalty of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 where circumstances are serious, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax amount; persistent non-payment can trigger tax enforcement measures, asset preservation, and restrictions on legal representative exit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payment Business Operation Report and Audited Financial Statements (non-bank payment institution annual regulatory filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) - local branch with supervisory jurisdiction over the licensed payment institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end, normally by March 31, or another date expressly notified by PBOC in licence conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission constitutes a licence condition breach that attracts PBOC rectification orders, regulatory interviews, suspension of part or all payment business operations, and in severe or repeated cases administrative revocation of the Payment Business License.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Statements Audit (certified CPA audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: A PRC-registered certified public accounting firm retained by the company; the audit report is maintained at the registered office and supplied to shareholders, SAMR, STA, and PBOC as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements must be prepared at year-end and the audit completed before the CIT settlement deadline of May 31 and, for payment institutions, before the PBOC compliance return deadline normally falling on March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have annual accounts audited by a lawful CPA firm violates the Company Law and the payment institution's licensing conditions; consequences include abnormal-operations listing, tax authority corrective measures, and PBOC rejection of the annual compliance submission or licence suspension.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption applies to resident PRC companies. Under the Company Law, every company must prepare annual financial accounting reports and have them audited by an accounting firm, so the audit trigger for this Sino-foreign equity JV is mandatory irrespective of size. For a licensed electronic-money/payment institution, PBOC rules independently require an annual independent CPA audit as a condition of the Payment Business License regardless of revenue or asset volume. An entity eligible for the Simplified Accounting System for Small Enterprises may use simplified CAS reporting, but the statutory audit obligation is not automatically waived.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (China GAAP / CAS) as issued by the Ministry of Finance; financial enterprises apply supplementary banking and payment institution accounting rules and PBOC statistical reporting standards. The CAS framework is substantially converged with IFRS, but IFRS are not the primary statutory filing basis in mainland China.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not maintain a public UBO registration form for ordinary private companies. The statutory mechanism is a shareholder register plus a change-registration system: any change to shareholders, directors, legal representative, registered capital, charges or pledges, or business scope must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the triggering event. In each annual enterprise information disclosure cycle, the entity must confirm registered shareholder capital contributions and legal representative details as at year-end. As a licensed payment institution, the entity must also identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owners of customer legal entities under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and retain CDD/UBO profile records for the applicable statutory retention period. No separate UBO annual confirmation return is filed to SAMR or PBOC, but the shareholder and AML registers must be accurate and available for on-site inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' meetings, board meetings, and supervisor meetings
AML/client UBO identification and CDD records (required of licensed payment institutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 2,500 per year for a standard compliant registered office address; USD 3,000 to USD 12,000 per year for a PBOC-notice-ready physical office in a major city such as Shanghai or Shenzhen
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 18,000 per year for a typical licensed EMI/JV; USD 15,000 to USD 35,000 or more where high transaction volumes, digital wallet reserve balances, and PBOC scope require extended audit procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture that qualifies as a High and New Technology Enterprise may enjoy a reduced 15% preferential rate. Additional incentives include an immediate additional 100% research and development super-deduction for qualifying R&D expenses, a 10% rate for certain resident enterprises engaged in encouraged digital finance or software/IC sectors meeting specific conditions, and carryover of unused losses for up to 10 years for qualifying high-tech or small and medium sized technology enterprises. Standard general enterprises retain a 5-year carryforward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (A-Type) / Form A, filed through the Chinese Electronic Tax Bureau (e-filing portal). Quarterly provisional returns are filed using the same portal on Form 16A (Quarterly Corporate Income Tax Return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional filings are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter. The final annual CIT return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (May 31 for calendar-year taxpayers), accompanied by the annual audited financial statements and the related-party transaction reporting schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basic taxpayer information: legal name, unified social credit identifier, tax registration number, registered address, industry classification, country of incorporation, and enterprise type (equity joint venture).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Chinese legal entity is a resident taxpayer because it is incorporated in mainland China; all worldwide income must be reported. Where non-resident shareholders own the JV, this box does not convert the entity into a non-resident return. However, cross-border shareholding and place-of-effective-management information must be disclosed in the schedule of related parties to allow the tax authority to assess permanent establishment and CIGA exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis and fiscal year: cash or accrual basis, calendar or non-calendar fiscal year, and accounting standards adopted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use accrual accounting; financial statements must conform to Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises. If the foreign parent consolidates but does not operate in China, no PE return is required for the parent solely as a shareholder. The JV must separately track intra-group management fees, recharges, and intercompany loans because deductibility will be challenged under tin capitalization and actual-service tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue: sales of goods, provision of services, and other business income. For an electronic money institution, this includes transactional fees, interchange fees, account servicing fees, foreign-exchange conversion margins, and interest earned on customer reserve floats.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all income from PRC sources and foreign sources unless treaty exempt. Do not net customer pass-through balances against fee revenue. Cross-border settlement fees earned from non-resident counterparties may be apportioned; the taxpayer must maintain a transfer pricing study showing that the JV retains profit commensurate with the functions it actually performs and the risks it actually assumes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs and deductions: operating costs, administrative expenses, financial expenses, taxes other than CIT, depreciation and amortization, and allowances for impairment losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions will be disallowed if the corresponding payment to a non-resident parent, affiliate, or group service company is not considered arm's length, lacks commercial substance, or is not documented with valid invoices. Interest on shareholder loans exceeding the statutory debt-to-equity ratio is non-deductible and is treated as a deemed dividend. Royalty or management-fee payments must be supported by a cost-benefit analysis and evidence of actual services. Expenses incurred outside China must be allocated under the reasonable allocation method and are subject to tax authority adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, non-taxable income, and adjustments that reduce taxable income: interest income from government bonds, qualified resident-to-resident dividends, and other statutory exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Chinese JV receives dividend distributions from other resident Chinese companies, those dividends are exempt under CIT Law Article 26. Such exempt income must nevertheless be disclosed. Dividends or profit distributions received directly or indirectly from overseas group companies are not automatically exempt; treaty relief may be relevant, and the non-resident recipient must prove beneficial ownership. Any exempt income that relates to illegal or unreported financial flows must be recharacterized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: addition of non-deductible expenditures, reduction of exempt income, and netting of tax losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the critical transfer pricing adjustment box. Common additions include: (1) interest disallowed under thin capitalization because the JV's net debt-to-equity ratio exceeds the 2:1 statutory limit for non-financial enterprises; (2) management fees paid to a non-resident parent where no actual service was rendered; (3) royalties paid for intangible assets held by a non-resident shell entity that performs no development, enhancement, maintenance, protection, or exploitation functions; (4) differences caused by application of the transaction net margin method. Tax losses may be carried forward for 5 years for the JV; losses arising in an overseas branch cannot be offset against the JV's domestic income if the foreign tax credit is otherwise claimed under Article 23.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and preferential rate reductions: foreign tax credit, R&D super-deduction, high-tech enterprise 15% rate, qualified equipment and software deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are capped to the Chinese CIT payable on the same foreign-source income. In computing the cap, the overseas tax must be actually paid and substantiated by a foreign tax credit certificate. If the JV receives management or service fees from a related enterprise in a low-tax jurisdiction, the credit may be denied on the ground that the income is not genuinely foreign-source or that the arrangement lacks economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable computation: tax rate application, final tax due, quarterly prepayments, and additional tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate or the 15% preferential rate only if all documentation and the preferential tax registration have been filed. The quarterly prepayments are treated as credits. Any under-payment discovered on an audit will trigger daily late-payment interest at 0.05% per day from the original due date. If tax authority adjustments transfer profit to a non-resident, the corresponding deemed dividend is subject to 10% withholding tax unless a treaty rate is claimed and substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Schedule of Related Party Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contemporaneous disclosure of all related-party transactions with foreign shareholders and affiliates: loans, intangibles, management fees, treasury services, settlement infrastructure, and licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This schedule must be filed together with the annual return on the e-Tax portal. The report must identify each related party, its jurisdiction, the transaction category, the transaction amount in RMB, and the transfer pricing method used. Failure to file the related-party schedule is a separate administrative violation. For an EMI, the reserve-management and virtual-IBAN settlement flows are treated as financial-asset transfers and must be disclosed even if no cash moves across the PRC border on a gross basis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000, rising to RMB 10,000 for serious non-compliance, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. The tax authority may impose an additional late-payment penalty of 0.05% per day and an administration fine between 50% and 5 times of the underpaid tax if the underpayment results from intentional concealment or false documentation. Fraudulent tax evasion with a large amount and a high proportion of underpaid tax triggers criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines. The company and the responsible director may be jointly and severally liable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholders must claim treaty benefits through the Chinese withholding agent at the time of dividend distribution. The protocol requires: (1) submission of a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the home jurisdiction tax authority covering the relevant calendar year; (2) a signed declaration that the shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividends and is not a conduit or nominee; (3) completion of the Non-Resident Taxpayer Enjoyment of Treaty Benefits Information Reporting Form (National Tax Public Notice [2019] No. 35); (4) evidence that the shareholder has the power to use and enjoy the income and bears the associated risks; and (5) retention and production of all underlying contracts, board minutes, and bank statements for a minimum of 10 years. A withholding agent that applies a reduced treaty rate without valid substantiation is jointly liable for the shortfall, late-payment interest, and penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties paid to non-resident enterprises is 10%; on interest paid to non-resident enterprises it is also 10%. Under China's bilateral tax treaties, treaty rates may be reduced to 5% or 10%, and interest paid to an unrelated financial institution may benefit from a zero rate under certain treaties. A reduced rate is available only where the beneficial owner is resident in the treaty jurisdiction and the payment is not deemed to be excessive or non-arm's length. Royalties for the use of intangibles are scrutinized for the DEMPE functions and the actual substance of the licensor; if the licensor is a shell entity, the royalty is recharacterized as a disguised dividend or profit distribution subject to the full 10% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous local file and master file preparation is triggered when any of the following related-party transaction amounts are exceeded in a fiscal year: tangible asset transfers above RMB 200 million; intangible asset transfers above RMB 100 million; financial asset transfers including loans, deposits, and virtual wallet reserve placements above RMB 100 million; other related-party transactions above RMB 40 million. Master file is additionally required where the enterprise and its related parties have cross-border related-party revenue exceeding RMB 1 billion or meet the thresholds under SAT Public Notice [2016] No. 42.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China adopts the substance-over-form doctrine and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Under the BEPS framework, an electronic money institution must demonstrate that its Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are performed in China or in the jurisdiction where profits are reported: strategic management of customer reserves, credit and settlement risk control, compliance and AML decision-making, negotiation and execution of SEPA and central-bank clearing contracts, and treasury management of digital wallet float. If a JV merely holds contracts and accounting records while decisions are made abroad, the tax authority may recharacterize the arrangement, attack the residency of the entity, deny treaty benefits, impose withholding tax on deemed distributions, and levy penalties. A Chinese JV must maintain real employees, physical and digital substance, board autonomy, and auditable evidence of all core activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Artificial Margin Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fictitious management fees, service charges, or royalties to a non-resident parent or shell affiliate when no actual service is rendered, no genuine asset is developed, and the dominant purpose is to reduce Chinese taxable income and shift profit out of China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority invokes the General Anti-Avoidance Rule and the Transfer Pricing Adjustment Rules, assessing additional taxable income, applying the 10% withholding tax on the recharacterized deemed dividend, imposing late-payment interest at 0.05% per day, and issuing a penalty of 50% to 5 times of the underpaid tax under the Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63. If the amount is significant, criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 201 applies, with a fine and imprisonment of not more than 7 years for especially large amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil where the JV is de facto a mere instrument of the foreign shareholder and the directors knowingly executed fraudulent invoices or circular payment schemes. Directors become personally liable for the unpaid tax arrears, are subject to civil restitution of diverted funds, may be placed on the tax-authority blacklist with a travel ban, and may face imprisonment for tax evasion. Criminal fines are imposed on the company and the responsible director individually.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell / Conduit Structure and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting an intermediate holding company in a tax-treaty jurisdiction with no economic substance, no real employees, no independent decision-making, and no meaningful activity other than collecting dividends, royalties, or interest from the Chinese JV, all to secure a reduced DTA withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority denies treaty benefits under the Beneficial Ownership rules and General Anti-Avoidance Rule, recharacterizing the intermediate company as a pure conduit. It imposes the full 10% statutory withholding tax, or the higher tax if the immediate shareholder is in a non-treaty jurisdiction, together with late-payment interest and a penalty ranging from 50% to 5 times of the shortfall. The transaction may be recast as a direct distribution to the ultimate shareholder and adjusted accordingly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the conduit structure and executed the dividend routing can be held personally liable for restitution of the underwithheld amounts. Chinese courts may lift the veil where the conduit is found to be abusive and the directors acted beyond good faith. The individuals are subject to personal asset freezing, travel restrictions, blacklisting from holding board positions in Chinese licensed financial institutions, and criminal prosecution under the Tax Collection Administration Law and Criminal Law if fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Fintech/EMI Operation and AML Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an electronic money or virtual IBAN service in mainland China without the required non-bank payment institution license, accepting customer funds as disguised deposits, failing to segregate customer reserve funds from corporate treasury balances, and deliberately obfuscating beneficial ownership information to avoid cross-border tax disclosure and AML checks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) imposes rectification and revocation of any ancillary license, confiscation of illegal gains, and administrative fines. Under the Anti-Money Laundering Law, serious violations carry fines from RMB 1 million to RMB 10 million and suspension or closure of business. Unlicensed absorption of public funds triggers criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 176 for illegally absorbing public deposits, with imprisonment of up to 10 years and fines. Tax implications include disallowance of all deductions tied to the illegal business, full CIT assessment at 25% on gross profits, and felony-based disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers are subject to personal asset freezing, travel bans (blacklisting), and prohibition from serving in financial institutions. The corporate veil is pierced when the directors commingle customer reserve funds into operating capital or use the JV as a facade for capital flight. Personal civil restitution is ordered for losses caused to customers and the State. Criminal imprisonment may be imposed for illegal deposit-taking, money laundering, or deliberately orchestrating offshore tax fraud through the unlicensed payment platform.
